questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: You need to set up a new Google Cloud project for a production workload. Your enterprise security policy mandates that all resources created in this project must reside within a specific geographical region to comply with data residency laws. How should you enforce this?

options.text: Write a startup script that verifies the region of every created resource and deletes non-compliant ones.
Set up a Cloud Monitoring alert that triggers a notification when a resource is created in an unauthorized region.
Apply an Organization Policy using the constraint `constraints/gcp.resourceLocations` at the project level.
Configure Cloud IAM roles to restrict users from accessing APIs in unauthorized regions.

questions.explanation: Google Cloud Organization Policies allow administrators to centrally configure restrictions on GCP resources. The `constraints/gcp.resourceLocations` constraint allows you to specify allowed resource locations, ensuring compliance with data residency requirements at the platform level before resources are provisioned.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Startup scripts run inside VMs and cannot prevent non-compliant resources from being created across the entire project, nor can they reliably enforce policy before resource provisioning.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Cloud Monitoring alerts are reactive and notify you after a non-compliant resource has already been created, failing to prevent the policy violation.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Cloud IAM manages authorization for who can perform actions on resources, but it does not restrict resource placement or geographical locations.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: Your company uses Google Workspace and you need to grant a temporary external auditor access to view logs in Cloud Logging for a specific project without granting persistent administrative access. What is the most secure way to provision this access?

options.text: Assign the `roles/logging.viewer` role to the auditor's email address at the project level.
Disable Identity-Aware Proxy and configure basic Viewer access on the project dashboard.
Grant the auditor project-level Owner access using their personal email address for the duration of the audit.
Create a new shared service account, export the private key, and securely send it to the auditor.

questions.explanation: To follow the principle of least privilege, you should assign the most restrictive role necessary to complete the task. The `roles/logging.viewer` role provides read-only access specifically to Cloud Logging data without granting broader project permissions.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Project Viewer grants read access to all resources and metadata within the project, which is broader than necessary for log viewing, and disabling IAP does not address role assignment.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Project Owner is an overly permissive role that grants full administrative control over all resources in the project, violating the principle of least privilege.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Sharing service account private keys introduces significant security risks, lacks auditability tied to a specific individual, and violates security best practices.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: You are managing multiple Google Cloud projects grouped under a single folder in your organization hierarchy. You need to apply a network firewall rule that blocks outbound traffic to a known malicious IP address range across all projects within this folder. Which approach should you use?

options.text: Deploy a single Cloud NAT gateway at the folder level to filter outbound traffic.
Create individual VPC firewall rules in every VPC network across all projects in the folder.
Configure a Hierarchical Firewall Policy at the folder level with a deny rule for the target IP range.
Modify the default VPC route tables in each project to drop packets destined for the malicious IP range.

questions.explanation: Hierarchical firewall policies enable centralized security management. By applying policies at the folder level, you can enforce rules that apply to all VPC networks within projects contained in that folder, ensuring consistent security baselines.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Cloud NAT provides source NAT for instances without external IP addresses; it is not designed to function as a centralized firewall policy enforcement point across multiple projects.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Manually creating individual firewall rules across every VPC is operationally inefficient, prone to configuration drift, and difficult to maintain.
wrongOptionNotes.D: VPC routes determine the next hop for packets, but they cannot drop packets based on destination IP ranges in the way firewall rules or hierarchical firewall policies can.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: You are provisioning a new Google Cloud project and need to associate it with your existing organization resource. However, you do not have permission to move the project to the organization. Which IAM role do you need to be granted to perform this action?

options.text: Project Mover (`roles/resourcemanager.projectMover`) on both the project and the target organization/folder
Billing Account Administrator (`roles/billing.admin`) on the billing account
Folder Admin (`roles/resourcemanager.folderAdmin`) on the parent folder
Project Creator (`roles/resourcemanager.projectCreator`) on the organization

questions.explanation: Moving a project into or across an organization hierarchy requires the `roles/resourcemanager.projectMover` role on the project being moved and on the source and destination parent resources.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Billing Administrator roles manage financial aspects and billing associations, but they do not grant permissions to modify the Resource Manager hierarchy.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Folder Admin manages folders and projects within a specific folder, but moving a project into an organization requires permissions at the organization level or specific project mover roles.
wrongOptionNotes.D: The Project Creator role only allows users to create new projects, not to move existing projects into an organization node.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: Your finance department requires a dedicated billing alert mechanism. When project spending exceeds 80% of the allocated monthly budget, an automated webhook must trigger a workflow in an external incident management system. How should you configure this?

options.text: Create a Budgets & Alerts configuration in Google Cloud Billing, set a threshold of 80%, and link it to a Cloud Pub/Sub topic that triggers your webhook consumer.
Write a daily Cloud Function triggered by a Cloud Scheduler job that queries BigQuery billing exports and calls the webhook.
Configure a VPC Service Controls perimeter around the billing API and route alerts through a secure proxy.
Set up a Cloud Monitoring alert policy based on the billing metric and attach a webhook notification channel.

questions.explanation: Google Cloud Billing Budgets allow you to define threshold rules (such as 80%). You can configure these budgets to publish notification messages to a Cloud Pub/Sub topic. From there, Pub/Sub can integrate with Cloud Functions or push subscriptions to trigger external webhooks.

wrongOptionNotes.B: While BigQuery exports provide detailed billing data, querying them daily introduces latency and duplicates built-in Cloud Billing budget notification capabilities.
wrongOptionNotes.C: VPC Service Controls protect against data exfiltration by securing APIs within a perimeter, but they do not generate budget alerts or webhook integrations.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Cloud Monitoring does not directly ingest granular billing metric data for custom metric-based alert policies in the way Google Cloud Billing budgets do.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: An external contractor needs to be granted read-only access to a specific Cloud Storage bucket containing public documentation assets. To follow enterprise security guidelines, you want to grant this access using a Google Cloud console-friendly method without creating a managed user account in your Cloud Identity domain. What is the best approach?

options.text: Set up a Cross-Organization Service Control policy allowing the contractor's entire organization access to your project.
Configure the bucket to be completely public by disabling Public Access Prevention.
Grant the `roles/storage.objectViewer` role to the contractor's external email address directly on the Cloud Storage bucket using IAM.
Create a dummy user account in your corporate Google Workspace domain and share the password with the contractor.

questions.explanation: Google Cloud IAM allows you to assign roles directly to external Google accounts (e.g., personal Gmail or external Google Workspace emails) without provisioning internal corporate identities, maintaining both security and ease of administration.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Cross-organization access is typically managed via IAM or Domain Restricted Sharing, but granting broad organization-wide access violates least privilege.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Disabling Public Access Prevention to make a bucket public exposes all objects to anyone on the internet, which violates security policies when access should be restricted to a specific contractor.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Sharing credentials violates security compliance and bypasses proper identity management.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: Your organization uses Domain Restricted Sharing (`constraints/gpc.domainRestrictedSharing`) to prevent data leaks. A developer needs to share a Cloud Storage bucket with a partner company that uses Microsoft Azure Active Directory for identity management. How can you provision access while complying with the constraint?

options.text: Create service accounts for every partner employee and export private keys.
Add the partner's Azure AD domain directly to the Google Cloud IAM policy as a trusted domain.
Federate your Google Cloud environment with the partner's Azure AD using Workload Identity Federation, and grant access to the federated principal.
Disable the Domain Restricted Sharing constraint globally for the duration of the project.

questions.explanation: Workload Identity Federation enables external identity providers (like Azure AD, AWS, or OIDC-compliant providers) to authenticate directly to Google Cloud. This allows secure access for external partners without violating Domain Restricted Sharing policies.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Creating multiple service accounts and distributing private keys is a severe security anti-pattern.
wrongOptionNotes.B: IAM policies accept Google accounts, Google Workspace domains, and service accounts, but cannot natively ingest external Azure AD domains directly into standard IAM bindings without federation.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Disabling security constraints globally compromises the security posture of the entire organization and violates compliance rules.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: You have deployed several Compute Engine instances across two different projects under the same folder. You need to ensure that administrators can manage IAM policies for project A without having any permissions on project B. Which level of the resource hierarchy should you assign the IAM roles?

options.text: At the Organization level
At the Folder level
At the individual Project level for Project A
At the Billing Account level

questions.explanation: Google Cloud IAM follows an inheritance model. Roles granted at higher levels (Organization, Folder) propagate to all child resources. To isolate administrative permissions to a single project, roles must be assigned directly at that project level.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Assigning roles at the organization level grants permissions across all projects and resources in the entire organization, violating least privilege.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Assigning roles at the folder level would apply permissions to all projects contained within that folder, meaning administrators would have access to both project A and project B.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Billing account level roles control financial management and billing access, not project-level IAM administration.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: Your security team requires an audit trail of all administrative actions and resource creations across all projects within your Google Cloud organization. Where should you configure this logging export to ensure centralized long-term retention?

options.text: Create an aggregated log sink at the Organization level pointing to a centralized Cloud Storage bucket in a dedicated logging project.
Rely on the default Cloud Logging retention period of 30 days without configuring any sinks.
Stream logs from each Compute Engine instance using the legacy syslog daemon to an external server.
Configure individual log sinks in every project to export logs to local project-level Cloud Storage buckets.

questions.explanation: Cloud Logging allows you to create aggregated sinks at the Organization, Folder, or Billing Account level. An organization-level sink can capture all logs (including Admin Activity and Data Access logs) across all child resources and export them to a centralized destination such as Cloud Storage or BigQuery.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Default logs are deleted after their retention period (typically 30 days for audit logs) and do not provide long-term retention or centralized compliance storage.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Using syslog on individual VMs misses platform-level audit logs (Admin Activity logs) and managed service logs.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Managing log sinks individually in every project is cumbersome and inefficient as new projects are created.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: You are setting up a new Google Cloud environment for a sensitive financial application. You want to ensure that developers cannot attach external IP addresses to any Compute Engine instances in the development or production projects. How should you enforce this restriction?

options.text: Configure IAM bindings to remove the Compute Network Admin role from all developer accounts.
Delete the default VPC network in every project so instances cannot be created with external IPs.
Set up a Cloud Monitoring alert that sends an email whenever an external IP is attached.
Apply the Organization Policy constraint `constraints/compute.vmExternalIpAccess` at the folder or project level.

questions.explanation: Organization Policy constraints provide preventive guardrails. The `constraints/compute.vmExternalIpAccess` constraint can be configured to deny all VMs from acquiring external IP addresses, ensuring compliance with security baselines.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Removing network admin roles prevents network creation, but does not prevent developers with instance creator roles from launching VMs with external IPs.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Deleting the default network does not prevent users from creating custom networks that provision external IPs.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Alerts are reactive and do not prevent the provisioning of external IPs.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: Your company has acquired another organization, and you need to migrate several GCP projects from their organization into yours. What is a prerequisite step before you can successfully move a project into your organization?

options.text: All Cloud IAM roles assigned to users must be manually deleted before the move.
You must recreate all Compute Engine instances from scratch in the new project.
The project must have an active Cloud Billing account linked that is valid in the destination organization.
You must change the project ID to match your organization's naming convention.

questions.explanation: When moving a project across organization boundaries, you must ensure that the project is linked to an active Cloud Billing account accessible within the destination organization, or unlink billing before initiating the move.

wrongOptionNotes.A: IAM policies remain intact during a project move, though external principals may be affected if domain restricted sharing policies differ.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Moving a project preserves its resources, including Compute Engine instances, without requiring recreation.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Project IDs are globally unique and permanent; they cannot be changed after a project is created.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: You need to grant a group of data analysts permission to query datasets in BigQuery and read raw files from a specific Cloud Storage bucket. To adhere to security best practices, you want to create a custom IAM role. What should you consider when designing this custom role?

options.text: Custom roles are automatically updated by Google Cloud when new permissions are added to underlying services.
Custom roles bypass the limit on the number of IAM bindings allowed per project.
Custom roles can only be defined at the project level and cannot be reused across the organization.
Custom roles allow you to bundle specific granular permissions from multiple services into a single role, adhering to the principle of least privilege.

questions.explanation: Custom IAM roles allow you to bundle precise sets of permissions from various Google Cloud services. They can be created at the project or organization level, helping you enforce the principle of least privilege when pre-defined roles are too broad.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Custom roles are static collections of permissions and are not automatically updated when Google adds new service permissions.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Custom roles are subject to standard IAM policy size limits and binding quotas.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Custom roles can be created at either the project level or the organization level, with organization-level roles being reusable across all child projects.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: You are deploying a multi-tier web application in Google Cloud. You want to ensure that database instances residing in the private subnet can securely access Google Cloud APIs (such as BigQuery and Cloud Storage) without traversing the public internet. Which Google Cloud networking feature should you configure?

options.text: Private Google Access enabled on the private subnet
A dedicated Cloud VPN tunnel connected back to your corporate datacenter
External IP addresses assigned to each database instance
Cloud NAT gateways attached to the private subnets

questions.explanation: Private Google Access enables VMs in a VPC subnet that do not have external IP addresses to send traffic to Google APIs and services via internal IP addresses, keeping traffic within Google's secure network.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Cloud VPN connects a VPC to an on-premises network, which is unnecessary for reaching Google Cloud services internally.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Assigning external IP addresses exposes instances to the public internet, violating security best practices for private database subnets.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Cloud NAT allows private instances to reach the public internet, but traffic to Google APIs would still route externally unless configured specifically.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: Your development team requires access to a shared Google Cloud project. You want to ensure that all human users authenticate using multi-factor authentication (MFA) and corporate credentials federated via SAML. Where should this authentication policy be enforced?

options.text: In the project's VPC firewall rules by blocking unauthenticated traffic.
In Google Cloud Identity or Google Workspace using Context-Aware Access and SSO configuration.
In Google Cloud Billing by requiring verified identities.
In Google Cloud IAM by creating custom IAM conditions for MFA status.

questions.explanation: Authentication policies, including Single Sign-On (SSO) federation with third-party IdPs (like Azure AD or Okta) and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), are managed centrally in Cloud Identity or Google Workspace, not within Google Cloud IAM or VPC configurations.

wrongOptionNotes.A: VPC firewall rules operate at layers 3 and 4 of the OSI model and cannot enforce user authentication or MFA.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Billing accounts do not manage identity authentication or federation.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Cloud IAM manages authorization (what users can do), not authentication mechanisms like MFA or federation.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: You have created a new service account for a CI/CD pipeline running outside of Google Cloud (e.g., GitHub Actions) to deploy application updates. To follow security best practices, how should you authenticate this external pipeline to GCP without downloading long-lived service account JSON keys?

options.text: Open a firewall rule allowing SSH access from GitHub's public IP range directly to your project.
Configure Workload Identity Federation to allow GitHub Actions to exchange its OIDC token for temporary GCP credentials.
Generate a master service account key with Owner permissions and rotate it every 24 hours.
Embed the service account password directly in the GitHub repository secrets.

questions.explanation: Workload Identity Federation enables external workloads (such as GitHub Actions, AWS, or Azure) to securely access Google Cloud resources using short-lived credentials via OpenID Connect (OIDC), avoiding the security risks associated with managing and storing service account private keys.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Opening SSH access to the project network creates severe security vulnerabilities and does not solve service account authentication.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Relying on long-lived keys introduces unnecessary risk; Workload Identity Federation is the modern, keyless standard.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Service accounts do not use passwords, and storing credentials as plaintext secrets is a major security vulnerability.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: Your company uses a shared Google Cloud project for hosting internal applications. Team leads need the ability to manage Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies for their respective application service accounts without having full project-level permissions that could compromise other teams' resources. How should you fulfill this requirement while maintaining least privilege?

options.text: Grant the team leads the Security Admin role at the folder level.
Grant the team leads the Service Account Admin role scoped directly to the individual service accounts they manage.
Grant the team leads the Project IAM Admin role on the shared project.
Assign the team leads the Owner role on the shared project.

questions.explanation: To achieve least privilege when delegating management tasks for specific resources like service accounts, IAM roles should be bound directly to the target resource rather than at the project or folder level.

wrongOptionNotes.A: The Security Admin role at the folder level would apply permissions across all projects within that folder, far exceeding the intended scope.
wrongOptionNotes.C: The Project IAM Admin role grants full control over all IAM policies in the project, violating the principle of least privilege.
wrongOptionNotes.D: The Owner role provides complete administrative access to all resources and policies in the project, which is overly permissive.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: Your enterprise requires all Google Cloud billing data to be automatically exported to a BigQuery dataset for advanced cost analysis and custom reporting. You have already created a BigQuery dataset in your billing administration project. What is the next step you must perform in the Google Cloud Console?

options.text: Enable the BigQuery Data Transfer Service and configure a scheduled query to pull data from the billing API.
Navigate to the Billing section of the console, select 'Billing export', choose 'BigQuery export', and link your dataset.
Configure a Cloud Logging sink to route billing export logs into the BigQuery dataset.
Write a custom Cloud Function triggered by Cloud Pub/Sub to poll billing metrics and insert rows into BigQuery.

questions.explanation: Google Cloud Billing includes a native feature to export detailed cost data continuously to BigQuery, configured directly from the Billing management interface.

wrongOptionNotes.A: The BigQuery Data Transfer Service is not required for billing exports because the billing console has a direct, real-time export configuration.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Cloud Logging sinks are used for log entries, not for continuous automated billing data exports.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Building custom polling mechanisms is unnecessary since Google Cloud provides a built-in automated BigQuery billing export feature.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment

Where should you apply these constraints?

options.text: At the Organization node, using Organization Policies.
At the Folder level representing the specific business unit, using Organization Policies.
By writing custom IAM conditions on every project IAM binding.
At the individual Compute Engine instance level during creation.

questions.explanation: Organization Policies allow administrators to set restrictive constraints that apply recursively to all resources within folders and projects, aligning with the hierarchical structure of GCP.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Applying policies at the root Organization node would enforce them globally, which may conflict with other business units that require external IPs.
wrongOptionNotes.C: IAM conditions govern identity access control, whereas restrictions on resource configurations (like external IPs) are managed via Organization Policies.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Applying constraints manually per instance is prone to human error and does not scale or enforce organization-wide compliance.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: Your security operations team needs to receive immediate notifications whenever a new firewall rule is created or modified in any project within your organization. You want to implement an automated, scalable alerting mechanism. What is the recommended approach?

options.text: Assign the security operations team the Network Admin role across all projects so they can manually review the firewall rules daily.
Create a log-based alert in Cloud Logging that triggers when an audit log captures firewall modification events, and route it to a notification channel.
Write a cron job inside a virtual machine that periodically calls the Google Cloud API to list all firewall rules and compares them with a local backup.
Set up a Cloud Monitoring uptime check targeting the default VPC firewall endpoint.

questions.explanation: Cloud Logging paired with log-based alerts provides a robust, serverless mechanism to detect specific Admin Activity audit log events and alert administrators instantly.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Manual reviews do not provide immediate notifications and violate least privilege by granting broad administrative rights.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Polling APIs via a cron job is inefficient, non-scalable, and introduces significant latency compared to event-driven audit logging.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Uptime checks are designed to monitor network reachability and HTTP/TCP endpoints, not API mutations or configuration changes.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: You are deploying a new application in a Google Cloud project. Your security team requires that all data stored in Cloud Storage buckets within this project must be encrypted using a key that your company fully controls, rather than Google-managed keys. How should you satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Manually encrypt every file on your local machine using GnuPG before uploading them to Cloud Storage.
Use Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) via Cloud Key Management Service (Cloud KMS).
Disable default encryption on the bucket and rely solely on Identity and Access Management.
Use Customer-Supplied Encryption Keys (CSEK) where Google stores your secret key permanently.

questions.explanation: Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) via Cloud KMS give organizations administrative control over the lifecycle of keys used to protect data at rest in Cloud Storage.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Client-side manual encryption is cumbersome, breaks server-side indexing and searching features, and is not a scalable enterprise solution.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Google Cloud encrypts all data at rest by default; disabling encryption is not permitted, and IAM controls access rather than cryptographic security.
wrongOptionNotes.D: With CSEK, Google does not store your keys; you must provide the key with every API request, which is difficult to manage for standard storage operations.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment

Hardcoding personal Master API Keys inside the shared source code repository.
Google Cloud Shell
A shared Compute Engine instance with an attached high-privilege service account accessible via public SSH.

questions.explanation: Google Cloud Shell provides developers with a secure, transient, command-line environment equipped with pre-authenticated Google Cloud SDK tools.

wrongOptionNotes.A: User accounts do not support JSON key files, and sharing credentials via insecure channels violates basic security standards.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Hardcoding credentials is a critical security violation that exposes secrets if the repository is compromised.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Exposing a shared VM to the public internet with high privileges introduces severe security vulnerabilities and credential leakage risks.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment

options.text: Write a custom Python script that continuously downloads logs using the Cloud Logging API and uploads them to the bucket.
Create a sink at the Organization or Folder level pointing to the centralized Cloud Storage bucket, and grant the sink's service account Storage Object Creator permissions on the bucket.
Set up a Cloud Pub/Sub topic in the logging project and instruct all projects to publish log messages directly to it.
Configure individual logging sinks in every single project pointing to the same bucket, with no additional IAM configuration required.

questions.explanation: Aggregated log sinks placed at the folder or organization level capture telemetry from all descendent projects, simplifying centralized auditing when paired with proper destination bucket IAM bindings.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Cloud Logging natively supports aggregated sinks, eliminating the need to write custom ingestion scripts.
wrongOptionNotes.C: While Pub/Sub can be used for streaming logs, native aggregated Cloud Logging sinks provide a simpler and more direct export mechanism to Cloud Storage.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Without granting the respective sink service accounts write permissions on the target bucket, export attempts will fail with permission errors.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: You are managing a Google Cloud project and need to grant an external vendor access to query specific tables within a BigQuery dataset. Grant the Project Editor role and instruct the vendor to only open BigQuery.
Grant the BigQuery Data Viewer role at the project level.
Grant the BigQuery Data Viewer role directly on the specific dataset resource.

questions.explanation: IAM roles can be scoped directly to individual BigQuery datasets, ensuring fine-grained access control without exposing broader project resources.

wrongOptionNotes.B: The Project Editor role provides broad access to create, modify, and delete most resources across the entire project.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Granting the role at the project level gives the vendor access to all datasets in the project, violating the principle of least privilege.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: Your company's security policy requires that all Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) networks created across any project must be configured as 'Custom subnet mode' networks, preventing developers from accidentally creating legacy or automatic subnet networks. Configure an Organization Policy constraint that disables automatic subnet network creation.
Set up a nightly billing report to check if any automatic networks were created.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Relying on documentation does not prevent developers from mistakenly creating automatic mode networks.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment

By writing a Cloud Billing export query in BigQuery and setting up scheduled email reports.
In the Google Cloud Billing console under Budgets & alerts.
Inside the Google Cloud Console under Cloud Monitoring alerting policies.

questions.explanation: Google Cloud Billing provides native budgeting tools where administrators can define exact percentage thresholds (including forecasted or actual spend) to trigger email alerts and Pub/Sub notifications.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Native billing budgets and alert thresholds can be configured directly without building custom BigQuery alerting workflows.
wrongOptionNotes.D: While Cloud Monitoring tracks system metrics, budget limits and financial threshold rules are managed directly within the Cloud Billing interface.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: An external auditor needs temporary access to review compliance logs stored in a Cloud Storage bucket. Make the Cloud Storage bucket publicly readable on the internet for two days.
Create a temporary Google Cloud user account for the auditor and delete the account after two days.
Add the auditor's email address to the bucket's IAM policy with the Storage Object Viewer role.

wrongOptionNotes.C: Managing temporary user accounts for external parties adds administrative overhead and is prone to oversight.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Permanent IAM bindings do not expire automatically and would require manual removal after 48 hours.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
