wrongOptionNotes.C: Alerts are reactive notifications and do not prevent the creation of unlabeled resources.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Manual labeling relies entirely on human compliance and frequently results in untracked resources.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: You are migrating several legacy applications into a new Google Cloud project. You want to track resource utilization costs by department by assigning metadata key-value pairs to Compute Engine instances, Persistent Disks, and Cloud SQL databases. What feature should you use?

options.text: VPC Service Controls
Firewall Tags
IAM Roles
Resource Labels

questions.explanation: Labels are structured key-value pairs designed specifically for organizing and filtering resources for cost management and operational reporting.

wrongOptionNotes.A: VPC Service Controls establish security perimeters to mitigate data exfiltration risks, unrelated to cost categorization.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Firewall tags are specifically used to target network traffic rules on Compute Engine instances, not for billing or cost allocation.
wrongOptionNotes.C: IAM roles define permissions for principals, not metadata for cost allocation.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: You are managing a Google Cloud project and need to grant a temporary contractor permission to deploy infrastructure using Terraform. To follow best practices, you want to ensure that the contractor's access is restricted to a specific custom role that contains only the precise permissions needed for deployment, and nothing more. What should you do?

options.text: Create a custom IAM role containing only the necessary permissions, and bind it to the contractor's user account for that project.
Share your personal Google Cloud login credentials with the contractor.
Assign the predefined Project Editor role to the contractor.
Assign the Organization Administrator role at the project level.

questions.explanation: When predefined roles are too broad, custom IAM roles enable administrators to curate exact permissions tailored to specific tasks.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Sharing user credentials is a major security violation that compromises accountability and access control.
wrongOptionNotes.C: The Project Editor role grants broad access to modify nearly all resources, far exceeding the minimal permissions needed.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Organization Administrator is a top-level role that grants complete control over the entire enterprise hierarchy.

questions.domain: Setting up a Cloud Solution Environment
questions.question: Your company's security team mandates that no data can be exfiltrated from your core production Google Cloud project to external networks or unauthorized projects. You need to secure Google Cloud services within a security perimeter. Which feature should you implement?

options.text: Cloud CDN
Cloud NAT
HTTP(S) Load Balancing
VPC Service Controls

questions.explanation: VPC Service Controls establish secure perimeters around Google Cloud services to mitigate data exfiltration risks and enforce context-based access restrictions.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Cloud CDN is a content delivery network used to cache web content closer to users, not a security perimeter tool.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Cloud NAT provides outbound internet access for private instances, rather than enforcing security perimeters around Google-managed APIs.
wrongOptionNotes.C: HTTP(S) Load Balancing distributes incoming client traffic across backend instances, unrelated to preventing data exfiltration from managed services.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your company is planning to migrate a legacy monolithic application to Google Cloud. The application requires access to a shared persistent file system across multiple Compute Engine instances running in different zones within the same region. Which storage service should you select?

options.text: Cloud Storage bucket with uniform bucket-level access
Local SSD with RAID 0 configuration
Persistent Disk with ReadOnlyMany access mode
Filestore Enterprise tier

questions.explanation: Filestore is Google Cloud's managed file storage service for applications that require a POSIX file system interface and shared access from multiple instances. The Enterprise tier provides high availability and regional replication across zones.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Cloud Storage is an object storage service, not a POSIX-compliant file system, and cannot be mounted directly as a traditional shared file system for multiple instances without specialized drivers like GCSFuse.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Local SSDs are physically attached to the host machine running the specific VM instance and cannot be shared across multiple instances or zones.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Compute Engine Persistent Disks can only be attached in ReadWrite mode to a single instance at a time (except for multi-writer Persistent Disks which are restricted to specific clustering configurations and filesystems like OCFS2).

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: You are deploying a containerized web application to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). The application needs to dynamically scale based on HTTP traffic requests per second (RPS) rather than just CPU utilization. How should you implement this?

options.text: Increase the maximum node pool size in the GKE cluster configuration
Configure the standard Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) using CPU utilization metrics only
Deploy the Custom Metrics Horizontal Pod Autoscaler and use the Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus to query application request rates
Configure Cloud CDN to automatically scale the backend Kubernetes pods

questions.explanation: When applications require autoscaling based on metrics other than CPU or memory (such as custom HTTP request rates), you must use custom metrics adapters or integrations like the Managed Service for Prometheus combined with the Kubernetes HPA.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Scaling the number of cluster nodes manages infrastructure capacity, not individual pod replication based on application-level traffic metrics.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Standard HPA based solely on CPU will not scale based on custom application metrics such as HTTP requests per second.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Cloud CDN caches content at the edge and accelerates delivery, but it does not directly drive the autoscaling of GKE backend pods.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your development team needs to provision a managed relational database on Google Cloud for a new transactional web application. The database must automatically handle storage scaling and support high availability with automatic failover across zones. Which service should you choose?

options.text: BigQuery with auto-scaling slots
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL with high availability configuration enabled
PostgreSQL installed on a Compute Engine instance with a persistent disk
Bigtable with automatic node scaling

questions.explanation: Cloud SQL is the ideal managed service for relational databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server) requiring automated maintenance, backups, storage scaling, and regional high availability.

wrongOptionNotes.A: BigQuery is a serverless enterprise data warehouse designed for large-scale data analytics, not for low-latency transactional (OLTP) web applications.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Self-managing PostgreSQL on Compute Engine requires manual intervention for high availability setup, failover, patching, and disk resizing.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Bigtable is a NoSQL wide-column database designed for massive analytical and operational workloads, not a relational transactional database.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: You are designing the networking architecture for a multi-tier application on Google Cloud. The architecture requires that database instances reside in a private subnet with no external IP addresses, but they must still securely download software updates and patches from the internet. What is the most secure and recommended method to achieve this?

options.text: Attach ephemeral external IP addresses to the database instances during patch windows
Set up a public HTTP(S) Load Balancer in front of the database instances
Configure Cloud NAT in the VPC to allow outbound traffic to the internet without assigning external IP addresses to the instances
Route all database patch traffic through a bastion host using port forwarding

questions.explanation: Cloud NAT provides managed Network Address Translation, enabling instances in private subnets to communicate with the internet for updates and APIs without requiring public IP addresses.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Exposing database instances directly to the public internet via external IP addresses violates security best practices and increases attack surfaces.
wrongOptionNotes.B: A public load balancer handles incoming client traffic, not outbound traffic to third-party patch repositories.
wrongOptionNotes.D: While a bastion host provides administrative access, routing all system updates through it is inefficient, complex to scale, and unnecessary when managed NAT services exist.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your company stores sensitive financial documents in a Cloud Storage bucket. Compliance regulations dictate that these objects must not be modified or deleted by any user, including administrators, for a period of exactly 5 years. Which Cloud Storage feature should you configure?

options.text: Cloud Storage lifecycle management rules with a delete action set to 5 years
Bucket Policy Only (uniform bucket-level access)
Cloud Storage Bucket Lock with a retention policy locked for 5 years
Object Versioning with a noncurrent object retention policy

questions.explanation: Cloud Storage Bucket Lock uses retention policies to enforce WORM states. Locking the policy prevents even the project owner or administrators from deleting or modifying objects until the retention period expires.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Lifecycle management rules can delete objects after a certain time, but they can also be altered or deleted by administrators, failing strict immutability compliance requirements.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Uniform bucket-level access simplifies permissions by disabling ACLs, but it does not prevent object deletion or modification.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Object versioning keeps older versions when objects are overwritten, but administrators can still delete versions unless locked by specific retention controls.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: You need to deploy a batch processing job that runs nightly, processes large amounts of data stored in Cloud Storage, and terminates upon completion. The job can tolerate interruptions and needs to be as cost-effective as possible. Which Compute Engine configuration should you choose?

options.text: Always-on Compute Engine instances with custom machine types
Managed instance groups using standard pricing with automatic healing enabled
Preemptible virtual machines (or Spot VMs) managed by a custom instance group
Standard Compute Engine instances configured with sole-tenant nodes

questions.explanation: Spot VMs (and predecessor Preemptible VMs) provide excess compute capacity at significantly reduced prices. They are best suited for batch processing and fault-tolerant workloads.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Always-on instances run continuously and incur standard rates, which is inefficient for a job that only runs nightly and terminates.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Standard pricing instances do not provide the maximum cost savings required for fault-tolerant batch jobs that can utilize discounted spot capacity.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Sole-tenant nodes dedicate physical hardware solely to your project, which is expensive and meant for strict isolation or licensing compliance, not cost-effective batch jobs.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your security team requires that all data encrypted at rest in your custom Google Cloud resources must use encryption keys managed entirely by your organization on-premises, with Google having no access to the keys. Which encryption option should you implement?

options.text: Google-managed encryption keys (GMEK)
Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) using Cloud KMS
Default service account keys stored in Secret Manager
Customer-supplied encryption keys (CSEK)

questions.explanation: Customer-Supplied Encryption Keys (CSEK) give you full control over the keys protecting your data at rest in services like Compute Engine. Google does not store your CSEK keys on its servers.

wrongOptionNotes.A: GMEK keys are fully managed and stored by Google on your behalf.
wrongOptionNotes.B: CMEK allows you to manage keys within Cloud KMS on Google Cloud, but Google infrastructure still handles the keys during processing.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Secret Manager stores secrets and credentials, but it is not a direct block-level or object-level storage encryption mechanism for data at rest.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: You are managing a Google Cloud project with multiple departments. You want to delegate administrative permissions for managing IAM policies and resources strictly within a specific folder to the department lead, without granting them organization-wide privileges. How should you assign this access?

options.text: Assign the Resourcer Manager folder admin or appropriate IAM admin role at the specific folder level
Assign the Project Editor role at the organization root level
Grant the user billing administrator access across the entire billing account
Share the master Google account password with the department lead

questions.explanation: Google Cloud resource hierarchy allows IAM policies to be set at the organization, folder, project, and resource levels. Setting policies at the folder level scopes permissions to all child projects within that branch.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Assigning permissions at the organization root grants access to all projects and folders in the organization, violating the principle of least privilege.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Billing administrator access controls financial aspects and invoice management, not resource creation or IAM policy management inside folders.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Sharing account credentials violates basic security practices and bypasses Cloud Identity and IAM audit logging.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your web application experiences unpredictable traffic spikes. You have deployed an external HTTP(S) Load Balancer in front of a Managed Instance Group (MIG). Users report intermittent connection timeouts during peak traffic periods. Upon investigation, you notice that instances in the MIG are becoming overwhelmed before new instances can spin up and initialize. What should you do?

options.text: Switch the load balancer from external HTTP(S) to an internal TCP proxy
Disable autoscaling and fix the instance group size to a single large machine type
Increase the cool-down period of the Managed Instance Group autoscaler
Configure health checks with shorter check intervals and add autoscaler predictive scaling or adjust initialization periods and minimum capacity

questions.explanation: Proper autoscaling configuration requires balancing minimum capacity, health check responsiveness, and instance startup times to ensure new instances are ready to handle traffic before spikes overwhelm existing nodes.

wrongOptionNotes.A: An internal TCP proxy is meant for internal microservices, whereas external web applications require external HTTP(S) load balancing.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Fixing the size eliminates the benefits of horizontal scaling and does not resolve peak load capacity bottlenecks.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Increasing the cool-down period delays scaling actions even further, worsening timeout issues during sudden spikes.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your company uses Google Cloud Billing and needs to ensure that no single project exceeds a specific monthly budget threshold, and that automated notifications and resource shutdowns occur if spending spikes unexpectedly. What is the best way to implement this?

options.text: Set up Cloud Billing budgets with programmatic notifications tied to a Cloud Pub/Sub topic and a Cloud Function to disable billing or shut down resources
Manually check the billing dashboard every morning
Configure a quota increase request in the IAM console
Set up a standard VPC firewall rule to block traffic once budget is reached

questions.explanation: Cloud Billing budgets combine alerting thresholds with Cloud Pub/Sub integrations, empowering automated architectures (via Cloud Functions) to take action when spending approaches or exceeds limits.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Manual monitoring is reactive, prone to human error, and unable to prevent sudden cost overruns in real-time.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Quota requests manage resource limits (like max number of VMs), not financial spending thresholds.
wrongOptionNotes.D: VPC firewall rules control network traffic packets based on IP/ports, not project financial budgets.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your team is deploying a new microservice on Cloud Run. The service needs to connect securely to a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance that only has a private IP address within a VPC network. How should you configure Cloud Run to reach the database?

options.text: Deploy a dedicated Compute Engine VPN gateway to tunnel traffic between Cloud Run and Cloud SQL
Assign a public IP address to the Cloud SQL instance temporarily
Configure Cloud Run VPC connector (Direct VPC egress or Serverless VPC Access) to route traffic to the VPC network
Route all database queries through an external HTTP(S) load balancer

questions.explanation: Cloud Run VPC egress features (such as Serverless VPC Access or Direct VPC egress) allow serverless services to send traffic into a VPC network to reach internal IPs like Cloud SQL instances.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Cloud Run is a managed serverless platform and cannot terminate VPN tunnels directly; instead, it uses built-in VPC connector features.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Exposing the database with a public IP introduces security risks and violates the requirement that the database only use private IPs.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Load balancers handle HTTP/HTTPS traffic, whereas database connections use specific protocols (like PostgreSQL wire protocol over TCP), making HTTP load balancing inappropriate.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: You have a large volume of historical log data (approx. 50 TB) stored in Cloud Storage. You need to run ad-hoc ANSI SQL queries against this data without provisioning servers, managing databases, or maintaining indexes. Which Google Cloud service is best suited for this task?

options.text: Cloud SQL for MySQL with federated storage engines
Firestore with compound indexes
BigQuery with an external table pointing to Cloud Storage
Dataproc cluster running Apache Hive

questions.explanation: BigQuery external tables enable direct querying of data stored in Cloud Storage, Google Drive, or Bigtable using standard SQL, providing serverless analytics without data movement.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Cloud SQL is an OLTP database poorly suited for ad-hoc analytical queries over 50 TB of unstructured file logs.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Firestore is a NoSQL document database designed for transactional app state, not large-scale log analytics.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Dataproc requires managing Hadoop/Spark clusters and nodes, whereas the requirement specifies avoiding server and cluster provisioning.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your organization requires that all Google Cloud resources must be deployed within a specific region (e.g., us-central1) to comply with data residency laws. Any attempt to create resources in other regions must be automatically blocked. What is the most effective policy control to implement?

options.text: An organization policy utilizing the 'Constraints/Resource Location Restriction' constraint
A custom VPC firewall rule blocking traffic destined for foreign regions
Daily manual audits of the Cloud Asset Inventory export
IAM custom roles assigned to all project members restricting location parameters

questions.explanation: The Organization Policy Service provides centralized governance. The `constraints/gcp.resourceLocations` constraint is specifically designed to enforce compliance mandates by restricting resource creation to approved regions.

wrongOptionNotes.B: VPC firewall rules filter packet-level network traffic, not the API-level creation of compute or storage resources in different regions.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Manual audits are reactive and do not actively block unauthorized resource creation in prohibited regions.
wrongOptionNotes.D: IAM roles control permissions on APIs and services, but they do not enforce granular geographic constraints or parameter validation across resource creation.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: You are deploying a web application on Compute Engine. The application requires high availability, automatic distribution of incoming traffic across multiple instances, and SSL certificate termination at the load balancer. Which load balancing architecture should you select?

options.text: External TCP/UDP Network Load Balancer
Internal TCP/UDP Load Balancer
Standalone HAProxy instance running on a Compute Engine VM
External Application Load Balancer (HTTP(S) Load Balancer)

questions.explanation: External Application Load Balancers (HTTP/HTTPS) provide layer 7 capabilities, including SSL offloading, global/regional anycast IP addressing, and advanced traffic distribution to backend instances.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Network Load Balancers operate at layer 4 (Transport layer) and do not support HTTP/HTTPS features like SSL certificate termination or URL-based routing.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Internal load balancers are designed for internal private traffic between backend tiers within a VPC, not for public internet-facing web applications.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Self-managing HAProxy on a VM creates a single point of failure and lacks the native Google Cloud scalability and management benefits of managed load balancers.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your company's security policy states that service accounts used by applications running on Compute Engine must have the minimum necessary permissions. A particular application only needs to read objects from a specific Cloud Storage bucket and write logs to Cloud Logging. How should you assign permissions?

options.text: Create a dedicated service account and grant granular predefined roles such as Storage Object Viewer and Logs Writer
Attach the primitive 'Project Owner' role to the service account
Disable IAM checks for the service account by granting it unrestricted access
Attach the primitive 'Project Editor' role to the service account

questions.explanation: Best practices dictate creating dedicated service accounts for applications and assigning the most granular predefined roles possible (such as Storage Object Viewer and Logs Writer) rather than broad primitive roles.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Project Owner grants full administrative control over the entire project, which is a major security risk for application service accounts.
wrongOptionNotes.C: IAM checks cannot be disabled for service accounts, and granting unrestricted access is insecure.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Project Editor grants broad read/write access to almost all resources in the project, violating the principle of least privilege.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your analytics team is planning to ingest a continuous stream of clickstream data from a global mobile application into Google Cloud for real-time processing and storage. The solution must automatically scale and decouple the data ingestion layer from the processing pipeline. Which Google Cloud service should you choose for the ingestion layer?

options.text: Cloud Storage
Compute Engine with Apache Kafka
Cloud Pub/Sub
BigQuery

questions.explanation: Cloud Pub/Sub is the native Google Cloud service for real-time messaging and stream ingestion. It provides automatic scaling and decouples message producers from consumers, which is ideal for high-throughput global mobile applications.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Cloud Storage is designed for object storage, not for streaming real-time event ingestion with decoupled messaging semantics.
wrongOptionNotes.B: While Kafka can handle streaming, deploying and maintaining it on Compute Engine introduces operational overhead when a fully managed serverless alternative like Cloud Pub/Sub is available.
wrongOptionNotes.D: BigQuery is an enterprise data warehouse designed for SQL analytics, not for handling raw stream message ingestion and producer-consumer decoupling.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your company operates an e-commerce platform hosted on Google Cloud. You need to provision a managed relational database that supports horizontal read scaling globally while ensuring strict ACID compliance for transactional write operations. Which database service best fits this requirement?

options.text: Firestore
Bigtable
Cloud SQL
Cloud Spanner

questions.explanation: Cloud Spanner is the only enterprise-grade, globally distributed relational database service that combines ACID transactional guarantees with horizontal scale.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Firestore is a NoSQL document database designed for mobile and web app backends, offering flexible data models and limited transactions, but it is not a traditional relational database with global horizontal write scaling.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Cloud Bigtable is a wide-column NoSQL database designed for massive analytical and operational workloads, but it does not support full relational SQL queries or multi-row ACID transactions across complex schemas.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Cloud SQL is a fully managed relational database service (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server) that scales vertically and supports regional read replicas, but it does not provide globally distributed horizontal write scaling natively.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: You are designing a data archival architecture where data must be stored securely for at least 3 years to meet regulatory compliance requirements. The data will rarely be accessed—perhaps once a year. Cost minimization is the primary factor. Which storage class should you select?

options.text: Nearline Storage
Standard Storage
Coldline Storage
Archive Storage

questions.explanation: Cloud Storage Archive is the cheapest storage class, tailored for data accessed less than once a year. It has a 365-day minimum storage duration requirement, fitting the 3-year compliance scenario perfectly.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Nearline Storage is designed for data that you intend to read or modify an average of once per month, making it too expensive for multi-year archival with annual access.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Standard Storage is optimized for frequent data access and high performance, making it the most expensive choice for long-term infrequent archives.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Coldline Storage is low-cost storage for data that is intended to be read or modified at most once a year, but its storage pricing is higher than Archive Storage.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your team needs to design an internal web portal that will be accessed exclusively by employees connected via an interconnect from your corporate headquarters. The application should not be exposed to the public internet. What is the correct load balancer architecture to achieve this?

options.text: External HTTP(S) Load Balancer
Internal HTTP(S) Load Balancer
Network Load Balancer
TCP Proxy Load Balancer

questions.explanation: Internal HTTP(S) Load Balancing is a regional, software-defined managed service that allows you to run and scale your internal HTTP(S) services behind private IP addresses.

wrongOptionNotes.A: An External HTTP(S) Load Balancer assigns public IP addresses and accepts traffic from the public internet, which violates the requirement to keep the portal internal.
wrongOptionNotes.C: A Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 and can be internal, but for an HTTP/HTTPS web portal requiring URL-based routing and Layer 7 features, an Internal HTTP(S) Load Balancer is appropriate.
wrongOptionNotes.D: A TCP Proxy Load Balancer terminates TCP sessions externally and is intended for global TCP traffic routing, not internal HTTP(S) enterprise web portals.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: You are managing a shared Google Cloud environment with distinct development, staging, and production folders. You need to assign the 'Compute Instance Admin' role to a junior engineer, but their responsibilities are strictly limited to the development project. According to Google's best practices, where should you apply this IAM binding?

options.text: At the organization node
At the staging and production folder level
Directly on the development project resource
Globally across all folders using billing accounts

questions.explanation: IAM policies should be granted at the lowest level possible (principle of least privilege). Assigning the role on the specific development project ensures the user cannot affect staging or production environments.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Applying a role at the organization node grants permissions across all projects in the organization, violating the principle of least privilege.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Applying permissions at the folder level would inadvertently grant access to staging and production resources as well.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Billing accounts manage financial data, not IAM compute permissions, and a global assignment violates least privilege.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your enterprise organization requires all new Google Cloud Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) networks to be created in 'Custom subnet mode' rather than 'Automatic subnet mode' to maintain strict IP address allocation control. Which feature should you implement to enforce this policy automatically across the entire organization?

options.text: VPC Service Controls
Cloud IAM conditions
Organization Policy Service
Cloud Armor security policies

questions.explanation: The Organization Policy Service enables cloud administrators to configure centralized constraints (such as disabling automatic VPC creation) that apply to all projects within the organization hierarchy.

wrongOptionNotes.A: VPC Service Controls protect against data exfiltration by creating security perimeters around Google Cloud services, but they do not enforce VPC subnet mode configurations.
wrongOptionNotes.B: IAM conditions allow conditional access based on attributes like time or resource name, but they cannot enforce resource configuration constraints like subnet creation modes.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Cloud Armor provides web application firewall (WAF) and DDoS protection for load balancers, not infrastructure configuration enforcement.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: You are deploying a custom machine learning model on a Compute Engine instance. The model requires maximum computational throughput and low-latency floating-point calculations, and you need to attach a GPU. Which instance series and feature should you select?

options.text: A memory-optimized instance without networking capabilities
A standard micro instance with preemptible pricing enabled
A sole-tenant node with standard storage configurations
A general-purpose or compute-optimized instance with an attached NVIDIA GPU accelerator

questions.explanation: Compute Engine supports adding GPU accelerators to specific machine families to handle intensive workloads such as machine learning training, rendering, and high-performance computing.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Memory-optimized instances are designed for in-memory databases, and instances require networking capabilities to download dependencies and serve requests.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Micro instances have extremely limited CPU and memory resources and cannot support heavy machine learning models or GPU attachments.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Sole-tenant nodes provide physical hardware isolation for compliance, but they do not automatically provide GPU acceleration unless specifically provisioned with GPU-enabled machine types.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your development team needs to deploy an internal API service that scales up rapidly during business hours and scales completely down to zero instances during nights and weekends to minimize costs. The service is packaged as a standard container image. Which service is best suited for this requirement?

options.text: Cloud Run
Compute Engine Managed Instance Group
App Engine Standard Environment
Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Standard

questions.explanation: Cloud Run is designed specifically for running stateless containerized services serverlessly, offering rapid autoscaling and the ability to scale down to zero when idle.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Managed Instance Groups manage virtual machine instances and do not natively scale down to zero compute infrastructure costs instantly like a serverless container platform.
wrongOptionNotes.C: App Engine Standard supports scaling to zero, but it requires specific language runtimes and application structures, whereas Cloud Run accepts arbitrary container images.
wrongOptionNotes.D: GKE Standard clusters maintain underlying worker nodes that incur baseline costs even when pods are scaled down to zero, unless cluster autoscaling is configured with node auto-provisioning to zero (which still has management overhead compared to Cloud Run).

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: You are designing a disaster recovery strategy for a mission-critical relational database running on Cloud SQL. Your Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is near zero, and your Recovery Time Objective (RTO) must be minimal in the event of a regional infrastructure failure. What configuration should you implement?

options.text: Rely solely on automated backups scheduled every 12 hours
Create a regional read replica and promote it manually via command line
Take daily manual exports of the database to Cloud Storage
Configure a High Availability (HA) instance with automatic failover to a standby zone within the same region

questions.explanation: Cloud SQL High Availability (regional) instances maintain synchronous writes to a standby failover instance in another zone. If the primary zone fails, Cloud SQL automatically switches traffic to the standby instance.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Automated backups taken every 12 hours cannot guarantee a near-zero RPO or rapid recovery times.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Read replicas use asynchronous replication, leading to potential data lag, and manual promotion increases RTO compared to automatic HA failover.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Daily manual exports result in a 24-hour RPO, which fails the requirement for a near-zero RPO.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your company uses Google Cloud and wants to ensure that all team members receive alerts when cumulative project spending reaches 50%, 90% and 100% of a predefined monthly budget threshold. Which native tool should you configure?

options.text: Cloud Monitoring Uptime Checks
BigQuery billing export with custom Data Studio dashboards
Budgets & Alerts in Google Cloud Billing
Cloud Logging metric-based alerts on IAM policy changes

questions.explanation: Google Cloud Billing Budgets and Alerts provide native cost tracking and automated notifications when project spending reaches defined percentages of a target budget.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Cloud Monitoring Uptime Checks evaluate network endpoint availability, not financial budgets and cloud expenditure.
wrongOptionNotes.B: While BigQuery billing exports provide deep historical analysis, they require custom SQL queries and dashboard building, whereas native Budgets & Alerts provide out-of-the-box threshold notifications.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Cloud Logging alerts track log events like security changes, not financial spending thresholds.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: You are setting up a secure network environment in Google Cloud. You need to connect an on-premises datacenter to a Google Cloud VPC network with high throughput, encryption in transit across the public internet, and rapid provisioning. Which connectivity option should you choose?

options.text: External HTTP(S) Load Balancer with public peering
Cloud VPN (HA VPN)
Direct VPC peering
Dedicated Interconnect

questions.explanation: HA VPN provides a secure, encrypted IPsec connection between on-premises environments and Google Cloud over the public internet, supporting high availability and quick deployment.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Load balancers handle inbound internet web traffic, not secure site-to-site datacenter-to-VPC routing.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Direct VPC peering connects your internal network to Google's external network edge for services, but it is not a site-to-site VPN tunnel solution for private networks.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Dedicated Interconnect provides direct physical connections between your on-premises network and Google's network, but provisioning physical circuits takes weeks and does not encrypt traffic by default.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your security team mandates that all log data exported from your Google Cloud projects for long-term auditing must be centralized into a single Cloud Storage bucket located in a dedicated logging project. What is the correct method to export logs organization-wide?

options.text: Write a custom Python script running on Compute Engine to poll logs via API and upload them daily
Create an organization-level log sink with a destination pointing to the centralized Cloud Storage bucket
Configure individual log sinks in every project pointing to separate storage buckets
Use Cloud Monitoring to export metrics instead of log entries

questions.explanation: Cloud Logging allows you to create sinks at the organization, folder, or project level. An organization-level sink can route logs matching specific filters from all child resources directly to a centralized Cloud Storage bucket.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Writing custom polling scripts introduces maintenance overhead, potential latency, and unneeded complexity when native Cloud Logging log sinks exist.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Creating individual sinks in every project creates unnecessary operational overhead and fails to maintain a single centralized bucket efficiently.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Cloud Monitoring tracks numeric time-series metrics, whereas audit logs contain structured event records required for auditing.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your development team has written a Python application that needs to read and write objects to a specific Cloud Storage bucket. Following Google Cloud security best practices, how should you authenticate the application running on a Compute Engine instance?

options.text: Generate a JSON service account key, download it to the instance disk, and reference it in environment variables
Attach a custom service account with the 'Storage Object Admin' role to the Compute Engine instance
Embed the project owner's master password inside the application configuration file
Configure the Cloud Storage bucket permission to 'Public' so anyone can read and write without authentication

questions.explanation: Attaching a custom IAM service account directly to a Compute Engine instance is the standard, secure way to grant applications running on that VM access to Google Cloud services without managing static keys.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Manually downloading and storing static service account keys on disk is discouraged because keys can be leaked or stolen; attached service accounts manage credentials automatically and securely.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Hardcoding credentials or master passwords is a severe security violation that exposes resources to unauthorized access.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Making storage buckets public exposes sensitive enterprise data to the entire internet, violating security compliance.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: You are configuring firewall rules for a three-tier web application in a VPC network. You need to allow external HTTP traffic from the internet to your frontend web servers while blocking all direct inbound traffic to your backend database servers. Which configuration should you apply?

options.text: Create an ingress firewall rule allowing TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 targeted to instances with a 'frontend' tag, and ensure no ingress rule permits direct external traffic to the database tier
Attach a public IP address to every database server to filter packets via host firewalls
Create an egress firewall rule blocking all traffic leaving the database servers
Disable internal VPC routing between subnets

questions.explanation: Google Cloud VPC firewalls are implicit deny-inbound by default. You must create targeted ingress rules using network tags or service accounts to selectively permit authorized traffic while keeping internal tiers protected.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Attaching public IPs to internal databases increases attack surface and violates basic cloud security architecture principles.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Egress rules control outbound traffic, whereas the requirement specifies blocking inbound external traffic to the database.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Disabling internal routing would break legitimate communication between the frontend tier and backend tier.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your company is migrating an on-premises Hadoop analytics cluster to Google Cloud. You need a fully managed, serverless batch processing service that can execute Apache Spark jobs without requiring your team to manage virtual machine clusters or job scheduling infrastructure. Which service should you select?

options.text: Compute Engine with manual Spark installation
Dataproc Serverless
BigQuery Omni
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL

questions.explanation: Dataproc Serverless provides a managed environment to execute Spark workloads without cluster management, making it ideal for migrating Spark and Hadoop workloads effortlessly.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Installing and maintaining Spark on Compute Engine VMs requires manual cluster management, scaling, and operational overhead.
wrongOptionNotes.C: BigQuery Omni allows running analytics across multi-cloud storage, but it is not a native serverless Spark batch processing platform for migrated Hadoop jobs.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Cloud SQL is a relational database service, not a big data batch processing or Spark execution engine.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your company is planning to deploy a containerized microservices application to Google Cloud. The application requires Kubernetes orchestration, but your operations team lacks the capacity to manage the Kubernetes control plane, worker node provisioning, and software updates. Which service should you choose?

options.text: Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Autopilot mode
Compute Engine instances managed by a Custom Instance Template and Managed Instance Group
Cloud Run
Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Standard mode

questions.explanation: GKE Autopilot mode eliminates the operational overhead of managing nodes by automatically provisioning and managing the underlying compute infrastructure while providing a fully compliant Kubernetes API.

wrongOptionNotes.B: This option uses virtual machines and does not provide native Kubernetes orchestration features out of the box.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Cloud Run is a fully managed serverless platform for containerized applications, but it does not support native Kubernetes APIs or multi-container pod architectures in the same manner as GKE.
wrongOptionNotes.D: While GKE Standard manages the control plane, your operations team still has to manage the worker node instances, OS updates, and scaling configurations explicitly.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: You are designing the network topology for a multi-tier enterprise deployment on Google Cloud. You need to connect a central shared VPC host project to multiple service projects across different departments while ensuring fine-grained access control and IP address management. What is the recommended approach for setting up this architecture?

options.text: Deploy a Cloud VPN gateway in each service project connecting to the central project
Use VPC Network Peering between each department project and the central network
Create independent VPC networks in each project and use internal TCP/UDP Load Balancing across projects
Implement Shared VPC, enabling the host project administrator to share specific subnets with service projects

questions.explanation: Shared VPC enables organizations to share subnets from a single host project with service projects, allowing seamless internal communication and centralized network administration.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Cloud VPN tunnels introduce unnecessary routing complexity, latency, and throughput limitations for intra-cloud communication between projects within the same organization.
wrongOptionNotes.B: VPC Network Peering connects networks directly but does not support centralized administration or shared subnets as effectively as Shared VPC, and it does not scale well for multi-project administrative boundaries.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Cross-project internal load balancing adds overhead and complexity compared to Shared VPC, which natively allows services in different projects to communicate securely using internal IP addresses.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your finance department needs to analyze a massive, multi-terabyte dataset stored in Cloud Storage using standard SQL queries without provisioning or managing any underlying database or cluster hardware. Which Google Cloud service should you implement?

options.text: BigQuery with external tables defined over Cloud Storage
Bigtable
Dataproc
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL

questions.explanation: BigQuery supports querying data directly from Cloud Storage using external tables, enabling serverless SQL analytics over raw data files without provisioning cluster infrastructure.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Cloud Bigtable is a NoSQL wide-column database designed for low-latency, high-throughput operational workloads, not for running standard ad-hoc SQL queries.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Dataproc provides managed Hadoop and Spark clusters, which require cluster provisioning and management, violating the requirement for a serverless experience.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Cloud SQL is a fully managed relational database service designed for transactional workloads (OLTP) with fixed storage limits, not for ad-hoc petabyte-scale analytical queries over external files.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: You are configuring IAM policies for a project that handles sensitive customer data. Your security policy dictates that principals should only be granted the minimum necessary permissions to perform their specific tasks. Which best practice should you follow when assigning roles?

options.text: Assign basic roles (Owner, Editor, Viewer) at the project level to simplify permission audits
Create custom roles or use predefined roles assigned at the most granular resource level possible
Assign the Project Editor role to all developers to ensure they are never blocked
Use service accounts with owner permissions for all application integrations

questions.explanation: The principle of least privilege requires granting only the specific permissions needed by utilizing predefined or custom roles scoped tightly to the necessary resources.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Basic roles are broad and provide excessive permissions across all services in a project, violating the principle of least privilege.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Granting Project Editor permissions broadly introduces significant security risks and violates organizational compliance standards.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Service accounts should be assigned granular predefined roles specific to their required tasks, never owner permissions.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your team is deploying a new web application on Compute Engine. You need to ensure that incoming HTTP and HTTPS traffic from the public internet is allowed to reach your web server instances, while all other inbound traffic is blocked. How should you configure the firewall rules?

options.text: Create an ingress firewall rule with source IP range 10.128.0.0/9 and allow all ports
Disable the default VPC firewall and attach public IP addresses directly to every instance without rules
Create an ingress firewall rule with target tags, source IP range 0.0.0.0/0, and allow TCP ports 80 and 443
Create an egress firewall rule with destination IP range 0.0.0.0/0 and allow TCP ports 80 and 443

questions.explanation: Ingress firewall rules control incoming traffic to virtual machine instances. To allow public web traffic, you configure an ingress rule allowing traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 on ports 80 and 443.

wrongOptionNotes.A: A source range of 10.128.0.0/9 covers internal private IP ranges, not the public internet, and allowing all ports does not restrict traffic to HTTP and HTTPS.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Disabling or bypassing firewall rules leaves instances unprotected and violates GCP security best practices.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Egress rules control outbound traffic leaving your instances, whereas incoming traffic from the internet requires ingress rules.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your organization operates a global web application hosted on Google Cloud. You need to provision a global load balancing solution that terminates SSL/TLS connections at the edge, provides integrated content caching, and routes users to the closest backend instance based on their geographic location. Which service should you select?

options.text: External Regional Application Load Balancer
Classic VPN with static routing
Internal TCP/UDP Load Balancer
Global External Application Load Balancer

questions.explanation: Global External Application Load Balancers provide global Anycast IPs, SSL termination at the edge, Cloud CDN integration, and proximity-based routing for HTTP/HTTPS traffic.

wrongOptionNotes.A: An External Regional Application Load Balancer operates within a single region and does not provide global Anycast IP routing or global edge termination.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Classic VPN is a network connectivity service for connecting sites, not a load balancing solution for web traffic.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Internal TCP/UDP Load Balancers are regional and designed for private, internal traffic within a VPC network, not for global external HTTP/HTTPS traffic.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your company is migrating a legacy document storage system to Google Cloud. Standard Storage

Nearline Storage

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: You are deploying a custom web application across a Managed Instance Group (MIG) on Compute Engine. You need to ensure that the autoscaler adds or removes virtual machine instances based on actual workload metrics such as CPU utilization, rather than arbitrary time schedules. How should you configure the autoscaling policy?

options.text: Manually update the instance template size parameter whenever traffic increases
Set up a Cloud Scheduler cron job to execute resizing commands every hour
Configure the MIG autoscaler to target an average CPU utilization percentage across the group
Rely solely on preemptible VM instance termination notices to trigger automatic scaling

questions.explanation: Managed Instance Group autoscalers automatically adjust the number of instances based on metrics such as average CPU utilization, load balancing capacity, or Cloud Monitoring metrics.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Manual scaling requires continuous operator intervention and fails to provide automated elasticity.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Cloud Scheduler cron jobs do not dynamically react to real-time workload fluctuations and traffic spikes.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Preemptible VM termination notices only indicate that a specific VM is being reclaimed by Google Cloud, not whether overall application traffic requires scaling up or down.

questions.domain: Planning and Implementing a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your development team is creating a new serverless backend on Google Cloud using Cloud Run. The service needs to securely connect to a Cloud SQL PostgreSQL database instance that resides within a private VPC network with no public IP address. What is the recommended method to enable this secure connectivity?

options.text: Assign a public IP address to the Cloud SQL instance and restrict access via authorized networks
Configure Cloud Run to connect to the VPC network using Serverless VPC Access connector
Set up a public internet proxy server on a Compute Engine instance to bridge the connection
Use an external HTTP(S) Load Balancer configured with a backend bucket pointing to Cloud SQL

questions.explanation: Serverless VPC Access connectors allow serverless compute environments like Cloud Run to securely connect to private internal resources within a VPC network without using public IP addresses.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Exposing a database with a public IP address increases security risks and violates compliance requirements for private database architectures.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Introducing a custom proxy server adds operational overhead, maintenance burden, and potential security vulnerabilities.
wrongOptionNotes.D: External HTTP(S) Load Balancers cannot load balance traffic directly to Cloud SQL database instances in this manner.

questions.domain: Ensuring Successful Operation of a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your production application running on Compute Engine instances in a managed instance group (MIG) is experiencing intermittent HTTP 500 errors. You need to investigate the system logs and application error traces aggregated across all instances in the MIG without SSHing into each individual virtual machine.

options.text: Stream the logs from each instance disk manually using serial console output viewing via the Cloud Console.
Configure the Cloud Logging agent on the instances and query the logs centrally in the Cloud Logging Logs Explorer.
Set up a Cloud Monitoring uptime check to trigger an email notification whenever an HTTP 500 error occurs.
Export the Compute Engine disk snapshots to BigQuery and write SQL queries to search for error strings.

questions.explanation: Centralized log management using the Cloud Logging agent allows administrators to collect and query logs from multiple Compute Engine instances in a single interface (Logs Explorer) without needing direct SSH access to individual VMs.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Serial console logs only show boot and kernel messages, not application error traces.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Uptime checks only confirm availability and response codes, they do not provide log aggregation or debugging traces.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Snapshots capture block storage point-in-time states and are inefficient for real-time log analysis.

questions.domain: Ensuring Successful Operation of a Cloud Solution
questions.question: You manage a critical MySQL database running on a Cloud SQL instance. Recently, application traffic has spiked, and queries are running slowly. You need to identify the top resource-consuming queries immediately without modifying the application code.

options.text: Enable Cloud SQL Query Insights to identify which queries are consuming the most CPU and execution time.
Enable general query logging and parse the text logs manually in Cloud Logging.
Install the Cloud Monitoring agent on the Cloud SQL instance operating system.
Increase the machine type size of the Cloud SQL instance to instantly optimize bad SQL queries.

questions.explanation: Cloud SQL Query Insights is built specifically to analyze database performance, helping administrators diagnose slow queries, inspect query plans, and trace bottlenecks without altering code or managing underlying OS agents.

wrongOptionNotes.B: General query logs generate massive volumes of text data that are extremely inefficient to parse manually for performance troubleshooting.
wrongOptionNotes.C: You cannot install agents directly onto the underlying operating system of managed Cloud SQL instances.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Scaling up hardware is a costly workaround and does not address poorly optimized database queries.

questions.domain: Ensuring Successful Operation of a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your team deploys updates to a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster using a Deployment. During a recent rollout, a new version caused a crash loop, and the update halted. You need to inspect the failure reason and events associated with the failing Pods.

options.text: Delete the entire GKE cluster and recreate it using a previous stable cluster snapshot.
Restart the Google Cloud CLI tool to clear cached Kubernetes credentials.
Run kubectl describe pod [POD_NAME] to view recent events and container termination statuses.
Connect to the Google Cloud Console and inspect the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) flow logs.

questions.explanation: The 'kubectl describe pod' command is the primary troubleshooting tool in Kubernetes for checking container exit codes, readiness/liveness probe failures, and detailed event logs.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Recreating a cluster is destructive and completely unnecessary for diagnosing a failed Pod deployment.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Credential caching issues prevent authentication, but they do not cause or diagnose Pod crash loops.
wrongOptionNotes.D: VPC flow logs record IP network flows, not Kubernetes container lifecycle events or application errors.

questions.domain: Ensuring Successful Operation of a Cloud Solution
questions.question: You manage a Google Cloud Storage bucket storing sensitive financial reports. Compliance requirements dictate that you must be alerted immediately whenever a user downloads or deletes an object from this bucket.

options.text: Enable bucket versioning to ensure deleted objects can always be recovered.
Configure Cloud Audit Logs combined with a log-based metric and a Cloud Monitoring alert.
Write a cron job on a Compute Engine instance to poll the bucket contents every minute using gsutil.
Set up a Cloud Monitoring alerting policy based on the Storage Read and Storage Write metrics.

questions.explanation: Cloud Audit Logs record administrative activities and data access. By filtering for Cloud Storage data access logs (such as object reads and deletions), you can create log-based metrics and trigger real-time alerts.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Versioning protects data against accidental deletion, but it does not provide alerting or audit tracking.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Polling is inefficient, introduces high latency, and fails to capture user action audit details reliably.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Cloud Monitoring metrics provide aggregate usage rates, not granular per-object or per-user audit events.

questions.domain: Ensuring Successful Operation of a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your company runs a multi-tier application on Compute Engine. You need to create an automated backup strategy for persistent disks attached to stateful production instances to ensure recovery in case of regional disasters.

options.text: Configure Backup and DR Service or Compute Engine snapshot schedules (Snapshot Policies) to automate recurring snapshots.
Manually create a full disk snapshot via the Cloud Console at the end of every business week.
Write a bash script using gsutil to copy raw disk block data to a Cloud Storage bucket every night.
Attach an additional secondary persistent disk to every instance and mirror data in real time.

questions.explanation: Compute Engine snapshot policies automate the creation of incremental backups for persistent disks, ensuring reliable recovery points while minimizing storage costs.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Manual backups do not scale, risk human error, and do not provide adequate recovery point objectives (RPO).
wrongOptionNotes.C: Copying raw disk blocks via bash scripts is error-prone, manually intensive, and lacks incremental backup efficiencies.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Disk mirroring protects against hardware failure of a single drive, but it does not protect against accidental deletion or regional disasters like automated snapshots do.

questions.domain: Ensuring Successful Operation of a Cloud Solution
questions.question: You are managing a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. Users report that a specific web service is intermittently timing out. You want to inspect CPU and memory utilization trends for the specific Kubernetes nodes hosting these pods over the last 7 days.

options.text: Run the kubectl top nodes command to view historical metrics.
Use Cloud Monitoring dashboards to analyze historical CPU and memory utilization metrics for the cluster nodes.
SSH into each cluster node and inspect the /var/log/syslog file.
Examine the Kubernetes cluster autoscaler logs in Cloud Logging.

questions.explanation: Cloud Monitoring provides native integration with GKE, automatically collecting time-series metrics such as CPU utilization, memory usage, and network traffic for cluster nodes and pods over extended retention periods.

wrongOptionNotes.A: kubectl top provides real-time resource usage only and does not store or display historical trends.
wrongOptionNotes.C: System logs do not maintain structured time-series CPU and memory performance metrics over a 7-day period.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Autoscaler logs show scaling events (node additions/removals), not detailed resource utilization trends.

questions.domain: Ensuring Successful Operation of a Cloud Solution
questions.question: An unmanaged Compute Engine instance running a legacy web application is occasionally running out of memory (OOM), causing the application to crash. You need to configure a monitoring alert that notifies your operations team immediately when the instance's memory utilization exceeds 90%.

options.text: Set up a budget alert in Google Cloud Billing.
Configure an uptime check on the instance public IP address.
Create an alerting policy using the native Compute Engine cpu/utilization metric.
Create a Cloud Monitoring alerting policy based on the Agent-reported memory utilization metric.

questions.explanation: Google Cloud hypervisor metrics track CPU, disk, and network for Compute Engine instances, but guest OS memory metrics require the installation of the Cloud Monitoring agent.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Billing budget alerts track financial spending thresholds, not technical resource performance.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Uptime checks test whether an endpoint responds over HTTP/TCP, but they cannot monitor internal memory metrics.
wrongOptionNotes.C: CPU utilization measures processor load, not memory usage.

questions.domain: Ensuring Successful Operation of a Cloud Solution
questions.question: You are reviewing the IAM permissions for your Google Cloud project. You notice that an external contractor was granted the 'Project Editor' role last month. Security policy dictates that you must verify whether this user actually performed any actions within the project during their tenure.

options.text: Check the Billing report to see if the user generated compute costs.
Review the Compute Engine serial port output logs.
Inspect the project's Deployment Manager history.
Query Cloud Audit Logs in the Logs Explorer to review all API calls made by the user's email address.

questions.explanation: Cloud Audit Logs maintain a comprehensive trail of all administrative and access actions taken within a Google Cloud project, allowing security administrators to audit user behavior.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Billing reports provide cost summaries, not granular user activity logs or API calls.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Serial port logs only display operating system boot and console messages.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Deployment Manager only logs infrastructure deployments managed through its specific service, not all general user API calls.

questions.domain: Ensuring Successful Operation of a Cloud Solution
questions.question: Your web application experiences predictable daily traffic spikes during peak business hours. You manage the backend using a Compute Engine managed instance group (MIG).
